findings: Each native renderer creates two shaders, links one program, and calls deleteShader on both after linking. A deleted attached shader may remain owned by its program until program deletion; cumulative created counts are not a leak metric.
Renderer.destroy is guarded and deletes textures, buffer and program, loses the WebGL2 context and reduces the canvas backing. Constructor failure loses the context before rethrow.

Prepared renderers are owned by a two-entry map before transfer. Replacement, abort and eviction destroy the unconsumed renderer; preparation tickets reject superseded completion. The runtime receives unique ownership and MasterPresentation.destroy removes the Phaser texture and destroys the renderer.

The lifecycle observer uses WeakRef plus create/delete/context-loss tracking. Shader active counts concern explicit deletion flags; live counts require real GC samples and comparison after identical-world return. Driver memory is outside the observation.
